newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq snaps winning streak and closes lower.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq snaps winning streak and closes lower.

text.p: After seven straight session of new all time highs, the Nasdaq Composite Index snapped its streak and moved slightly lower as investors took profits.
The Index closed off 3.35 to 1297.02, or 0.26 percent, but traders said the move was no cause for alarm.

"This market is not ready to give up yet," said Jack Bayer, managing director and head OTC trader at Oppenheimer & Co. "Yesterday, it looked like it would tank but it stayed higher and earlier today, the OTCs were down about six or seven points" but were able to move off their session lows.
"But you do have to be prepared for a shakeout at some point in time, we're in uncharted waters," he said.
Falling stocks outpaced advancing stocks 1978 to 2300 on unofficial volume of about 640 million shares.
Most-active Intel Corp shares rose 3-5/8 to 129-1/2 and touched a new high for the year of 129-5/8 during the session.
GT Interactive shares sunk almost 40 percent, or 4-3/4 to 7-3/4 after it warned of a poor fourth quarters.
U.S. Robotics Corp rose 3-1/8 to 76-7/8, erasing about half of yesterday's losses after news that its modems would be used in Hitachi PC Corp notebook computers.
